lede: The biggest item this week is the Telluride Regional Medical Center board meeting Wednesday, where — after an executive session — trustees will take public action on who leads the hospital in the near term; public comment is open at the top via Zoom, so this is one to show up for. Mountain Village also holds a Town Council meeting with a first reading of an ordinance that would restructure how affordable housing fees get set. Across the valley, HARC takes up a work session on a potential demolition and new construction at Rebekah Hall — the town-owned building where HARC itself meets — and the BOCC continues its discussion of a view-plain MOU tied to a 1999 Mountain Village settlement.

notable.stake: HARC reviews potential demolition of Rebekah Hall, a Town-owned historic property.
BOCC takes up constitutional amendments and a 1999 Mountain Village view-plain MOU.
Two public hearings: Curry PUD and a parcel subdivision — testimony accepted.
First reading of ordinance shifting affordable housing fees outside municipal code.
Board votes publicly on interim leadership of Telluride's regional hospital.
